links.comparator_used: Uncorrected model probabilities from the MIMIC-IV-trained models applied to eICU hospitals (Platt scaling with 30% labeled local data was also benchmarked)
links.outcome: Expected Calibration Error across 185 eICU hospitals
links.effect: Mean ECE fell from 0.071–0.085 to 0.027–0.037 with Bayesian prevalence correction, comparable to Platt scaling with 30% labeled data (ECE 0.022–0.024). AUROC was not significantly correlated with ECE.
links.tradeoff: Prevalence correction left ECE slightly above Platt scaling with 30% labeled data (0.027–0.037 vs 0.022–0.024), but it needs only the local mortality rate and no labeled target data. It corrects only the prevalence-driven share of miscalibration (about 55–65%).
links.quote: A closed-form Bayesian prevalence correction requiring only the local mortality rate, and no labeled target data, reduced mean ECE from 0.071–0.085 to 0.027– 0.037, comparable to Platt scaling applied with 30% labeled data (ECE = 0.022–0.024).
